summary:
Lunar Lens is an interactive lunar mission-planning platform designed to help users evaluate landing sites based on sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and terrain conditions, tailored for ease of use, readability, and combining NASA tools.

Built for NASA's Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge, Lunar Lens combines NASA/NAIF SPICE ephemeris data with Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) imagery and LOLA elevation models to calculate the Sun's and Earth's positions relative to the Moon's actual terrain horizon, accounting for mountains, crater rims, and lunar curvature.

Users can explore a 3D Moon, select historical or candidate landing sites, enter custom coordinates, and simulate different mission dates. Simple View provides intuitive visualizations and plain-language explanations for students and the public, while Detailed View offers precise measurements, terrain visualization, and scientific graphs for mission planners. Site Detail provides in-depth analysis of individual locations, including visibility timelines and landing-delay scenarios. Compare supports evaluating multiple locations through site selection and comparative analysis tools.

By integrating complex NASA datasets into one accessible platform, Lunar Lens helps users assess operational windows, anticipate power and communication limitations, and understand how changes in location or timing affect lunar exploration.
details:
What We Developed

Lunar Lens is an interactive web-based platform designed to make lunar landing-site exploration and mission planning more accessible, intuitive, and understandable.

Evaluating potential landing sites involves complex astronomical and geographic data, including sunlight availability, Earth visibility, lunar terrain, and changing mission conditions. Existing scientific tools can be difficult for students, educators, and non-experts to navigate. Lunar Lens addresses this challenge by bringing essential NASA datasets and interactive visualizations together in one user-friendly application.

How Lunar Lens Works

Our Python/FastAPI backend uses NASA/NAIF SPICE ephemeris data to calculate the Sun's and Earth's positions from selected lunar locations. Using Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA elevation data, Lunar Lens also calculates the surrounding terrain horizon, accounting for mountains, crater rims, and lunar curvature that may obstruct sunlight or direct communication with Earth.

Users can explore historical and potential landing locations, enter custom coordinates, and adjust mission dates and times to understand how conditions change.

The platform is organized into three main pages, each offering Simple and Detailed viewing modes:

  • Explore: Users navigate an interactive 3D Moon, discover landing sites, and visualize solar illumination and Earth visibility. Simple View provides an intuitive globe and accessible indicators, while Detailed View offers scientific measurements, map controls, and interactive visualizations.
  • Site Detail: Users examine individual locations through Sun/Earth positions, terrain-aware horizon views, visibility timelines, and mission conditions. Simple View presents clear explanations and key insights, while Detailed View provides numerical measurements, graphs, and advanced analysis.
  • Compare: Users evaluate up to three landing sites side by side to understand differences in sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and mission timing. Simple View emphasizes clear visual comparisons, while Detailed View provides more precise metrics and charts.

Additional features include custom coordinate selection, interactive timelines, landing-delay analysis, and exploration of how nearby locations may experience different illumination conditions.

Tools, Technologies, and NASA Data

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, CesiumJS, Three.js, HTML/CSS.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, SpiceyPy, and NumPy.
  • Scientific Data: NASA/NAIF SPICE kernels, DE440 ephemeris data, LRO LOLA digital elevation models, LROC lunar imagery, and NASA Moon Trek mapping resources.
  • Development and Deployment: GitHub for version control, Vercel for frontend hosting, and Render for backend hosting.
  • Hardware: Standard laptops, without specialized equipment.

Creativity and Technical Considerations

Lunar Lens combines terrain-aware astronomical calculations with accessible, dual-level visualization. Rather than assuming a flat horizon, the platform considers actual lunar topography when determining whether the Sun or Earth is visible from a selected location.

Its main innovation is presenting scientific information through both Simple and Detailed views across all three pages, allowing users to choose the level of complexity that suits their needs.

Our team considered scientific accuracy, lunar curvature and orientation, terrain resolution, computational performance, and accessibility. We balanced detailed calculations with intuitive navigation and clear visual communication to make the platform useful for both technical and nontechnical audiences.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Lunar Lens aims to bridge the gap between specialized NASA scientific resources and accessible lunar exploration.

For researchers and mission planners, it provides a way to examine sunlight availability, Earth communication windows, terrain-related visibility limitations, and alternative landing scenarios. For students, educators, and space enthusiasts, it transforms complex lunar science into an engaging, interactive experience.

Ultimately, Lunar Lens demonstrates how NASA's publicly available scientific datasets can be transformed into an intuitive platform that helps users understand how location, terrain, and mission timing influence lunar exploration and surface operations.
